decisions.latin: a timóre inimíci éripe ánimam meam
decisions.why: The *erípere* row: *arrancar* where a source is named, *libertar* where none is. Here the source is named (*a timóre inimíci*), so *arrancai*, as 16:13 *arrancai a minha alma do ímpio* and 56:4b. Tearing a soul out of fear is a stronger image than the Portuguese ear expects, but the Latin's verb is the snatching one (ἐξελοῦ), and *livrar* belongs to *liberáre*. The natural order puts the soul before the source (the Latin puts the source first); both orders are Portuguese, and this one ends the verse on *inimigo*, a paroxytone.

options.label: libertai
options.note: the row's other verb, the one that 'never fails'; 6:5 has it with no source

decisions.why: *Convéntus* is a gathering, a meeting (L&S); the Greek is συστροφή, a knot of men banded together. The psalter already spends *congregação* on *concílium malignántium* (21:17, D34), *assembleia* on *ecclésiam malignántium* (25:5, D34) and *ajuntamento* on *conventículum* (15:4b, the same Latin root). *Ajuntamento* keeps the three phrases apart and says a crowd drawn together, which is what the Latin says; it does not say plot. MS1932's *conspiração* and DM1962's *conspiração* (from the Hebrew *sod*) say the scheming the Greek hints at, but that is to explain. *Malignántes → malvados* (D24).

options.label: ajuntamento
options.note: draft — the root of 15:4b *conventículum*; kept apart from *congregação* and *assembleia*

options.label: conluio
options.note: says the band-together of συστροφή; interprets the Latin's plain 'meeting'

options.label: reunião
options.note: the plainest; heard as a business meeting

decisions.why: *Rem amáram* stands in apposition, with no link (LXX πρᾶγμα πικρόν; DRB 'a bitter thing'): either the drawn bow, or the whole deed, is called a bitter thing. The Hebrew has the bitter *word* as their arrow — not the Latin. Between commas the Portuguese keeps the Latin's loose apposition and leaves open what is bitter. MS1932's *o arco envenenado* turns the phrase into an adjective of the bow and adds poison; refused as paraphrase.

options.label: uma coisa amarga
options.note: the article supplied; one syllable more

decisions.why: *Sagittáre → flechar* (row, open; Ps 10:3). The formula row *intendérunt arcum … ut sagíttent* says Ps 63 copies 10:3's *armaram o arco … para flecharem*; done. *Assetear* would echo *setas* (63:8 *sagíttæ*) but is hardly said in Brazil.

options.label: assetearem / assetearão
options.note: MS1932's verb; keeps the root of *setas* in 63:8

decisions.why: The row *in ábditis / in occúltis* (open) gives *em lugares ocultos* (9:29, 16:12; ἐν ἀποκρύφοις, as here). There the phrase says where someone sits or dwells; here it goes with a verb of shooting, and *flecharem em lugares ocultos o imaculado* is heard as the victim hidden, not the archers. *Às ocultas* keeps the root and the hiding and says how they shoot; it is four syllables shorter on a colon already long. Departure from the row recorded; *às escondidas* is 9:30a's *in abscóndito*.

options.label: às ocultas
options.note: draft — the adverbial phrase; the root kept

options.label: de emboscada
options.note: MS1932 — explains the hiding as an ambush

decisions.why: *Immaculátus → imaculado* (row; 17:24, 18:8, 118:1), ἄμωμον. A blind reader once listed the word as unknown; others passed it. The masculine article keeps it from being heard as the Immaculate. MS1932 and DM1962 have *o inocente*, which is *ínnocens*'s word (9:29 *interfíciat innocéntem*).

options.label: o que é sem mancha
options.note: the row's option, as a clause

decisions.why: The plainer of two faithful words (D2). *De súbito* (MS1932) is correct and known, but bookish in speech; *de repente* is how Brazil says it. First place in the psalter; 72:19 *súbito defecérunt* will follow.

*Sibi* is a reflexive dative (ἑαυτοῖς): for themselves, or among themselves. *Para si* keeps the Latin's word; *entre si* says the agreement among plotters that the next verse (*narravérunt … dixérunt*) implies, and is more natural with *firmar* — but it decides for the reciprocal. *Sermo → palavra* (D15).

options.label: para si
options.note: draft — the dative as it stands

options.label: entre si
options.note: reciprocal: they sealed a word between them; decides the reading

decisions.why: *Nequam* is 'worthless, vile, bad' (L&S); the Greek is πονηρόν, the common word for evil. *Má* is the plainest and keeps the Greek's generality; it ends the verse on a stressed syllable. *Vil* keeps the Latin's own colour (worthless) but is less said. *Perversa* would take *pervérsus*'s word (17:27). *Maligna* would bring back the *malígnus* root that D24 moved to *malvado*. **v2:** the stylist found the monosyllable close weak and asked *perversa*; refused for the collision, kept as an option. An oxytone close is allowed.

options.label: perversa
options.note: the stylist: a fuller close than the monosyllable; refused — *perverso* is *pervérsus*'s word (17:27)

decisions.why: The Greek is διηγήσαντο τοῦ κρύψαι παγίδας, 'they told of / talked over hiding snares'; the Latin's *ut* + subjunctive is its rendering, between purpose and content. *Narraram como esconderiam laços* keeps *narrar* (row *narráre → narrar*) and the subjunctive's forward look, and is heard as 'they talked over how to hide snares', the sense DRB gives ('They have talked of hiding snares'). A purpose clause (*narraram, para esconder laços*) is the Latin's surface but is heard as 'they told stories so as to hide snares'. MS1932 *Convencionaram esconder laços* explains. **v2:** the Latinist (minor): *como* reads *ut* as 'how'; *que* (content) taken. The stylist asked *Contaram* for *Narraram*; kept as an option — the *narráre* row repeats across psalms, and the doubled r is not a trip in Brazilian speech. **v2 gate:** the Latinist now asks for draft 1's *como* (minor) — the opposite of the v1 run's fix. Held at *que*: the two runs contradict each other, both are minor, and neither Portuguese construction is the Latin's *ut* exactly; *que esconderiam* is DRB's 'talked of hiding', *como* is 'how'. For Gustavo's ear; one touch.

options.label: Narraram que esconderiam
options.note: v2 ruling — the Latinist: *como* narrows *ut* to 'how'; a content clause, DRB's 'talked of hiding'

options.label: Narraram como esconderiam
options.note: draft 1; the v2 gate asked for it back (minor) after the v1 Latinist had asked it away

options.label: Narraram, para esconder
options.note: the Latin's *ut* as purpose, to the letter

options.label: Contaram que esconderiam
options.note: the stylist's plainer verb; refused for the *narráre → narrar* row (18:2, 21:23)

decisions.why: The verse says one root three times (ἐξηρεύνησαν … ἐξερευνῶντες ἐξερευνήσει); the repetition is the Latin's (D2) and stays. *Scrutári → sondar* (row, open; 7:10, 118:2, 34, 69, 115, 129). *Esquadrinhar* (MS1932, and the row's option) is more vivid but four syllables and colloquial in Brazil ('rummage'). Whatever verb is chosen, the tail *scrutínio* follows it (decision `scrutinio`).

*Scrutínium* (L&S 'a search', citing this verse) is an ablative of the same root — the Hebrew-Greek intensive figure, 'searching with searching'. It can say that they gave out from searching so hard, or that they failed in their search (DRB 'they have failed in their search'). *De tanto sondar* is how Portuguese says the intensive, and keeps the root a third time; it leans to exhaustion, but *desfaleceram* itself holds both 'fainted' and 'failed'. *Na sondagem* keeps a noun but in Brazil *sondagem* is an opinion poll or a drill. *No seu sondar* keeps the sphere without leaning, at the cost of a bookish turn. **v2:** the Latinist (minor) found *de tanto* an intensive the Latin does not state; *no seu sondar* (option 1 of draft 1) taken — it keeps the root a third time and leaves failure and exhaustion open. The stylist had named draft 1's line the psalm's best, for the threefold root, which stays. **v3:** the gate (minor) found *seu* added; *no sondar* taken — the article and infinitive alone, as the bare ablative.

options.label: no sondar
options.note: v3 ruling — the Latinist at the v2 gate: *seu* is not in the Latin; the bare ablative

options.label: no seu sondar
options.note: v2 ruling — the Latinist: *de tanto* adds an intensive the bare ablative does not state

options.label: na sondagem
options.note: the Latinist's fix; *sondagem* is heard in Brazil as an opinion poll or a drilling

decisions.why: *Accédere* is *chegar* at 90:10 (*O mal não chegará a ti*) and *aproximar-se* at 33:6 (*Aproximai-vos dele*), where *appropinquáre* also has *aproximar-se*. *Chegará a* is shorter and says arrival, which the Latin's future says. The verse is famous for its openness (the plotter comes up against a deep heart; or man comes to a deep heart, and God is exalted — Augustine reads it of Christ): *o homem* keeps the subject as general as *homo*. **v2:** the Latinist (minor) read *chegará* as attainment where *accédet* is approach; taken. It also removes the vowel pile-up *chegará a um* the stylist heard.

options.label: se aproximará de
options.note: v2 ruling — the Latinist: *accédere* is to draw near, not to arrive; = 33:6

decisions.why: *Altus* is high or deep; the Greek is καρδία βαθεῖα, deep, and DRB has 'a deep heart'. *Um coração alto* would keep the Latin's echo *altum … exaltábitur* (*alto … exaltado*), but in Portuguese a 'high heart' is a proud one, the opposite sense. The echo is given up for the sense.

options.label: alto
options.note: keeps the echo with *exaltado*; heard as haughty

decisions.latin: Sagíttæ parvulórum factæ sunt plagæ eórum
decisions.why: Subject and predicate are both plural nominatives. The Greek marks the subject (αἱ πληγαὶ αὐτῶν, with the article): 'their wounds became children's arrows' — the blows they strike are as harmless as a child's. The Latin's order (arrows first) is kept: the ear then hears 'children's arrows became their wounds', which is the other reading the Latin's order allows (the wicked wounded by the little ones' arrows), and both say the plotters' weapons came to nothing. *Deles* rather than *suas*, so that the wounds are not heard as the children's. *Plaga* here is a wound (D39 left 63:8 to decide locally): *feridas* (MS1932, DRB 'wounds'); *golpes* would say the blows given. **v2:** the stylist named draft 1's order the worst line (parsed backwards; *deles … eles* at mediant and final) and the ambiguity reader could not say what it meant. Taken: order is grammar (D2), and the parse is the Greek's, which the Latin translates; the other reading was an accident of the Latin's word order more than a meaning it carries. Draft 1's order stays option 2.

decisions.why: The Latin's passive (ἐπαινεσθήσονται): the upright will be praised. Row *laudári → ser louvado* (33:3 *No Senhor será louvada a minha alma*; 62:12 has the same verb). MS1932 *serão louvados* agrees here. The Hebrew's 'will glory' (DM1962 *gloriar-se-ão*) is another sense. The verse is the martyrs' versicle and responsory (Commune C2, C2p, C2a-1).

The stylist found the enclitic on *Protegestes-me* at the head of the verse stiff and asked for the subject named with the proclitic, as 60:4 *Vós me guiastes* (the same request, taken there). A subject pronoun is grammar (D2). It also marks the verse as a statement after the imperatives of 63:2, which the ambiguity reader half heard as a plea.

options.label: Protegestes-me
options.note: draft 1; no pronoun, as the Latin

choices.63:2: *Exáudi → escutai* (D3); *cum déprecor → quando suplico* (*deprecári → suplicar*, D35), no object supplied, as the Latin. The Introit of 04-25 and the martyrs' Common open with this verse.
choices.63:3: *Protexísti* with the enclitic at the head of the verse (*Protegestes-me*); *operántium iniquitátem → dos que praticam a iniquidade* (row *operári iniquitátem*). The verse is the Paschaltide martyrs' Introit (*Protexísti me, Deus, a convéntu malignántium*).
choices.63:4: *exacuérunt → afiaram* (D44: *afiado* for an edge); *ut gládium → como espada* (v2: the stylist asked the article away; the Latin has none), with the object moved before the comparison, Portuguese order. *intendérunt arcum → armaram o arco* copies 10:3 (row). The second colon is long, as the Latin's is. Checks: +3 on the second colon, accepted.
choices.63:6: Ps 63:5 has no verse of its own in DO; the Latin numbers 63:4 then 63:6. *Sermo → palavra* (D15).
choices.63:6b: *Quis vidébit eos?* → *Quem os verá?* — *eos* can be the snares or the plotters, as in Portuguese.
choices.63:7b: *exaltábitur → será exaltado*, the future passive (17:47's *exalte-se* is a jussive). The first colon is +8 syllables in v2 (checks): *cor altum* is three Latin syllables, *um coração profundo* seven, and *se aproximará de* (the Latinist's fix, = 33:6) is longer than *chegará a*; no shorter faithful phrase was found. Accepted; the colon is still one breath.
choices.63:8: *infirmátæ sunt → se enfraqueceram* (17:37, 26:2b, 30:11b). *Contra eos* kept: their tongues grew weak against themselves. v2's order removes draft 1's *deles … eles* echo at mediant and final.
choices.63:9: *conturbáti sunt → perturbaram-se* (47:6); *omnis homo → todo homem*, verb first as the Latin and 38:12b. v2 (the stylist): *todos aqueles que os viam* for the stutter *os que os*; *e temeu todo homem* for a fuller close than the clipped *todo homem temeu*.
choices.63:10: *Et annuntiavérunt → E anunciaram* (D41); the initial *Et* kept. *facta → feitos*; *intellégere → entender*.
choices.63:11: The versicle and responsory of the martyrs (*Lætábitur justus in Dómino, et sperábit in eo. R. Et laudabúntur omnes recti corde*); each half reads alone. *speráre in → esperar em* (D36); *recti corde → retos de coração* (row). Second colon +4 (checks): *retos de coração* is the settled phrase.
choices.63:7: The second colon is +3 (checks): the participle *scrutántes* needs *os que sondavam*, and the root is kept a third time; accepted.

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from parallels (Latin, LXX, Hebrew, DRB, MS1932, DM1962). Liturgical uses found by grep in content/do: 63:2 in the Introit of 04-25 and Commune C2a-1/C2p and Quad6-5; 63:3 as the Paschaltide martyrs' Introit/versicle (*Protexísti me, Deus, …*); 63:11 as the martyrs' versicle and responsory (Commune C2, C2p, C2a-1; CommuneM). Hard readings: 63:4 *rem amáram* (apposition), 63:6b *narravérunt ut abscónderent*, 63:7 *scrutántes scrutínio* (the root three times), 63:7b *cor altum* (deep, with the lost echo of *exaltábitur*), 63:8 which nominative is the subject.

Hard checks pass. Soft: 63:4b +3, 63:7b +4, 63:7b first colon +5, 63:11b +4 — all accepted, reasons in choices. One rhyme flag, 63:8 *deles / eles*: the Latin has the same echo (*eórum / eórum*), accepted. Oxytone cadences at 63:6, 63:6b, 63:9b, 63:10a, 63:11b — allowed.
Read with latin.json. 3 minor, no major; all three taken.
